steps.look: Oblique coronal fluid-sensitive images from the greater-tuberosity footprint to the musculotendinous junction; oblique sagittal images for anteroposterior tear width; axial images for the upper subscapularis fibres.
steps.normal: Supraspinatus, infraspinatus, subscapularis and teres minor tendons intact, with normal thickness, signal and footprint attachment.
findings: Full-thickness supraspinatus tear at the footprint, __ mm anteroposterior, retracted __ mm [lateral to / at / medial to] the humeral head apex.
Partial-thickness [articular-sided / bursal-sided / intrasubstance] [ ] tear involving approximately __% of tendon thickness, __ mm long.
Tendinosis of the [ ] tendon: thickening and intermediate signal without a fluid-signal defect.
Tear of the upper subscapularis fibres [with / without] medial displacement of the long-head biceps tendon.
steps.tip: Magic-angle signal on short-TE images can mimic tendinopathy; confirm a defect on the long-TE fluid-sensitive sequence.

steps.look: The most lateral oblique sagittal T1 image on which the scapular spine joins the scapular body (the Y-shaped view); compare each cuff muscle with its fossa.
steps.normal: Normal bulk and signal of the rotator cuff muscles, without fatty infiltration or denervation oedema.
findings: Supraspinatus atrophy with a positive tangent sign.
Fatty infiltration of the [ ] muscle, [less fat than muscle / equal fat and muscle / more fat than muscle].
Oedema-like signal of the [supraspinatus / infraspinatus] muscle without a tendon tear, compatible with denervation; the [suprascapular / spinoglenoid] notch is [clear / contains a paralabral cyst].
steps.tip: Read the tangent sign on the most lateral Y-shaped sagittal image; more medial images make an atrophic muscle look fuller.

steps.look: Axial images from the superior labrum down the bicipital groove; oblique sagittal images through the rotator interval for the pulley; coronal images for the biceps anchor.
steps.normal: Long-head biceps tendon intact and located in the bicipital groove; biceps anchor and pulley unremarkable.
findings: Medial [subluxation / dislocation] of the long-head biceps tendon from the bicipital groove, with an associated upper subscapularis tear.
Tendinosis of the intra-articular long-head biceps tendon with [thickening / partial-thickness tear].
Empty bicipital groove compatible with long-head biceps rupture or tenotomy; tendon stump at [level].
Tear at the biceps anchor extending from __ to __ o'clock.
steps.tip: An empty groove on axial images is a dislocation until the tendon is found medially, anterior to, within or deep to the subscapularis.

steps.look: Axial images from superior to inferior using the glenoid clock face (3 o'clock anterior); ABER images for anteroinferior labral detachment when acquired; sagittal images for the glenoid contour and the axillary recess.
steps.normal: Glenoid labrum intact; capsule and glenohumeral ligaments unremarkable; no Hill-Sachs or osseous Bankart lesion.
findings: Anteroinferior labral tear from __ to __ o'clock [with / without] periosteal stripping ([Bankart / Perthes / ALPSA / GLAD] pattern) and [no / an] osseous glenoid fragment.
Hill-Sachs impaction of the posterosuperior humeral head, __ mm; glenoid bone loss __% by [method].
Humeral avulsion of the inferior glenohumeral ligament (HAGL): J-shaped axillary recess.
Posterior labral tear (reverse Bankart) with reverse Hill-Sachs impaction of the anterior humeral head.
steps.tip: Sublabral recess, sublabral foramen and Buford complex lie in the anterosuperior quadrant; they do not explain an anteroinferior labral defect.

steps.look: Coronal and sagittal images of the acromion, acromioclavicular joint and subacromial-subdeltoid bursa; superior axial images for an os acromiale; all planes for cartilage and effusion.
steps.normal: Glenohumeral cartilage preserved; no joint effusion; subacromial-subdeltoid bursa not distended; acromion and acromioclavicular joint unremarkable.
findings: Subacromial-subdeltoid bursal fluid, [small / moderate].
Acromioclavicular joint osteoarthritis with capsular hypertrophy and inferior osteophytes [contacting / not contacting] the supraspinatus musculotendinous junction.
Os acromiale at the [pre-acromion / meso-acromion / meta-acromion] level [with / without] oedema at the synchondrosis.
Glenohumeral cartilage loss, [focal / diffuse], with [osteophytes / subchondral change].

steps.label: Fracture map
steps.detail: Locate each malleolar fracture and relate the fibular fracture to the syndesmosis: Weber A below, B at, C above.
steps.look: Mortise and lateral views: follow the lateral malleolar cortex, then the medial malleolus, then the posterior tibial lip on the true lateral.
steps.normal: No fracture of the lateral, medial or posterior malleolus.
findings: Oblique fracture of the distal fibula at the level of the syndesmosis (Weber B), running anteroinferior to posterosuperior on the lateral view, displaced __ mm.
Transverse avulsion fracture of the lateral malleolus below the syndesmosis (Weber A) [with / without] a vertical medial malleolar fracture.
Fibular fracture above the syndesmosis (Weber C), __ cm above the joint line.
Posterior malleolar fracture involving approximately __% of the tibial articular surface on the lateral view, displaced __ mm.
steps.tip: Reconstruct the mechanism: a Weber B fibular fracture with a medial malleolar fracture or a widened medial clear space is a higher-stage, potentially unstable injury.

steps.label: Mortise and talar position
steps.detail: Check that the talus is centred in the mortise and compare the medial clear space with the superior clear space.
steps.look: True mortise view (about 15 degrees internal rotation) for clear spaces; lateral view for anterior or posterior talar subluxation.
steps.normal: Ankle mortise congruent; medial clear space equal to the superior clear space; no talar shift or tilt.
findings: Widened medial clear space of __ mm on the [mortise / stress] view, compatible with deltoid ligament injury and lateral talar shift.
Lateral talar shift of __ mm with an incongruent mortise.
Posterior subluxation of the talus with the posterior malleolar fragment.
steps.tip: The medial clear space should not exceed the superior clear space; widening without a medial malleolar fracture indicates deltoid ligament rupture.

steps.label: Syndesmosis and proximal fibula
steps.detail: Assess the distal tibiofibular relationship and decide whether the proximal fibula needs imaging.
steps.look: Mortise view for tibiofibular overlap and clear space; knee or full-length fibula view when a medial injury has no matching distal fibular fracture.
steps.normal: Distal tibiofibular relationship normal; no syndesmotic avulsion.
findings: Widening of the distal tibiofibular clear space, compatible with syndesmotic injury.
Avulsion fragment at the anterior tibial tubercle (Tillaux-Chaput) or the fibular attachment of the anterior tibiofibular ligament.
Medial injury without a distal fibular fracture; the proximal fibula is not included and a Maisonneuve fracture should be excluded.
steps.tip: A medial malleolar fracture or deltoid injury with an intact distal fibula should prompt a look at the proximal fibula (Maisonneuve injury).

steps.label: Articular surface
steps.detail: Describe plafond impaction, articular step or gap, posterior fragment size and talar dome injury.
steps.look: Lateral and mortise views for step and gap; CT sagittal and axial reformats when the posterior malleolus or plafond is involved.
steps.normal: Tibial plafond and talar dome congruent without step, gap or impaction.
findings: Intra-articular extension with __ mm step and __ mm gap at the [plafond / medial malleolus].
Impaction of the [anterior / posterior] plafond; CT would define the fragments for surgical planning.
Osteochondral fracture of the [medial / lateral] talar dome, __ mm.
steps.tip: The lateral radiograph underestimates the size and comminution of a posterior malleolar fragment; CT defines it.

steps.label: Associated findings
steps.detail: Check for dislocation, soft-tissue swelling, other fractures at the film edges and post-reduction alignment.
steps.look: The edges of every film: base of the fifth metatarsal, anterior process of the calcaneus and lateral process of the talus.
steps.normal: No dislocation; no additional fracture in the imaged foot and ankle; soft tissues unremarkable apart from swelling.
findings: Fracture-dislocation of the ankle with [lateral / posterior] talar dislocation.
Additional fracture of the [base of the fifth metatarsal / anterior calcaneal process / lateral talar process].
Post-reduction: mortise [restored / persistent talar shift of __ mm].
steps.tip: A fifth metatarsal base or anterior calcaneal process fracture can mimic an ankle sprain and hide at the film edge.

steps.label: Bones and osteochondral surfaces
steps.detail: Inspect the talar dome, tibial plafond and hindfoot for contusion, fracture, osteochondral lesion and accessory ossicles.
steps.look: Coronal and sagittal fluid-sensitive images for marrow oedema; coronal images for the talar dome; T1 images for fracture lines.
steps.normal: Normal bone marrow signal; no fracture or osteochondral lesion of the talar dome or tibial plafond.
findings: Osteochondral lesion of the [medial / lateral] talar dome, __ × __ mm and __ mm deep, [with / without] fluid signal at the fragment interface or subchondral cysts.
Bone marrow oedema of the [ ] compatible with contusion; no fracture line.
Fracture of the [lateral talar process / posterior talar process / anterior calcaneal process], seen as a T1-hypointense line.
Os trigonum with surrounding oedema and fluid, in keeping with posterior impingement in the appropriate clinical setting.
steps.tip: Fluid signal undercutting a talar osteochondral fragment, or cysts beneath it, suggests instability.

steps.label: Lateral ligaments and syndesmosis
steps.detail: Trace the anterior and posterior tibiofibular ligaments above the joint, then the anterior talofibular, calcaneofibular and posterior talofibular ligaments.
steps.look: Axial images from the tibial plafond (tibiofibular ligaments) down to the malleolar fossa (talofibular ligaments); coronal images for the calcaneofibular ligament deep to the peroneal tendons.
steps.normal: Anterior and posterior tibiofibular ligaments, anterior and posterior talofibular ligaments and calcaneofibular ligament intact.
findings: Complete tear of the anterior talofibular ligament at its [fibular / talar] attachment [with / without] a small avulsion fragment.
Thickened, wavy anterior talofibular ligament without discontinuity, in keeping with a chronic or healed sprain.
Tear of the anterior inferior tibiofibular ligament (syndesmotic injury) [with / without] interosseous membrane involvement.
Calcaneofibular ligament tear, indicating a more extensive lateral ligament injury.
steps.tip: The anterior talofibular ligament is seen at the level of the malleolar fossa; the tibiofibular ligaments lie higher, at the level of the plafond.

steps.label: Medial ligaments, sinus tarsi and plantar fascia
steps.detail: Assess the superficial and deep deltoid ligament, spring ligament, sinus tarsi and plantar fascia.
steps.look: Coronal and axial images for the deltoid layers; axial images beneath the talar head for the spring ligament; sagittal images for the sinus tarsi and plantar fascia.
steps.normal: Deltoid and spring ligaments intact; sinus tarsi fat preserved; plantar fascia of normal thickness and signal.
findings: Tear of the deep deltoid (posterior tibiotalar) ligament, [partial / complete].
Spring ligament thickening or tear [with / without] posterior tibial tendon dysfunction.
Replacement of sinus tarsi fat by oedema or fibrosis, compatible with sinus tarsi syndrome in the appropriate clinical setting.
Thickened proximal plantar fascia (__ mm) with perifascial oedema, compatible with plantar fasciitis.
steps.tip: The deep deltoid ligament normally looks striated because of interposed fat; this is not a tear.

steps.label: Tendons
steps.detail: Follow the medial flexors, peroneal tendons, anterior extensors and Achilles tendon from muscle to insertion.
steps.look: Axial images tendon by tendon: posterior tibial, flexor digitorum longus and flexor hallucis longus medially; peroneal tendons behind the fibula; extensors anteriorly; sagittal images for the Achilles.
steps.normal: Flexor, extensor, peroneal and Achilles tendons of normal calibre and signal; no tenosynovitis; peroneal retinaculum intact.
findings: Posterior tibial tendinosis with [enlargement / longitudinal split / attenuation] from the medial malleolus to the navicular insertion.
Longitudinal split tear of peroneus brevis at the retromalleolar groove [with / without] peroneal tendon subluxation.
Complete Achilles tendon rupture __ cm above the calcaneal insertion with a __ mm gap.
Tenosynovitis of the [ ] tendon sheath with fluid disproportionate to the joint.
steps.tip: The posterior tibial tendon is normally about twice the diameter of the flexor digitorum longus; fluid in the flexor hallucis longus sheath can communicate with the ankle joint.

steps.label: Joints, impingement and soft tissues
steps.detail: Assess effusion, synovitis, capsular thickening, impingement recesses, bursae, accessory muscles and masses.
steps.look: Sagittal images for the anterior and posterior recesses; axial images of the anterolateral gutter; sagittal images for the retrocalcaneal bursa.
steps.normal: No significant ankle or subtalar effusion; no synovitis; impingement recesses clear; bursae normal.
findings: Soft-tissue thickening in the anterolateral gutter, compatible with anterolateral impingement in the appropriate clinical setting.
Retrocalcaneal bursitis with [Haglund deformity / insertional Achilles tendinopathy].
Moderate tibiotalar effusion with synovial thickening.
Accessory muscle: [peroneus quartus / accessory soleus / flexor digitorum accessorius longus].
steps.tip: A small amount of joint fluid is physiological; call synovitis only when the synovium is thickened.

steps.label: Distribution
steps.detail: Describe which joints are involved and spared, symmetry, and proximal or distal predominance.
steps.look: Survey both hands and wrists joint by joint — DIP, PIP, MCP, carpus, radiocarpal and distal radioulnar — and any other joints included.
steps.normal: No joint-space loss, erosion or productive change in the imaged joints.
findings: Symmetric involvement of the MCP, PIP and wrist joints with relative sparing of the DIP joints (proximal, inflammatory distribution).
Predominant DIP and PIP involvement with the first carpometacarpal joint (osteoarthritis distribution).
Asymmetric involvement of DIP joints [in a ray distribution] with productive change (spondyloarthritis / psoriatic distribution).
Radiocarpal and second–third MCP predominance with chondrocalcinosis (CPPD distribution).
steps.tip: Distribution is the strongest single clue: rheumatoid arthritis is proximal and symmetric, erosive osteoarthritis central in the DIP and PIP joints, psoriatic arthritis distal and asymmetric.

steps.label: Joint spaces (cartilage)
steps.detail: Distinguish uniform from non-uniform joint-space loss and name the worst compartment.
steps.look: Well-centred PA views; compare the same joints on the prior study with the same projection and load.
steps.normal: Joint spaces preserved.
findings: Uniform joint-space narrowing of the [ ] joints, a pattern favouring inflammatory arthritis.
Non-uniform joint-space narrowing with osteophytes and subchondral sclerosis, favouring osteoarthritis.
Ankylosis of the [carpus / interphalangeal joints].

steps.label: Erosions, bone formation and density
steps.detail: Characterise erosions (marginal, central, overhanging edge), osteophytes, periostitis and periarticular mineralisation.
steps.look: Bare areas at joint margins (MCP joints and ulnar styloid), central subchondral bone and shafts for periostitis; judge periarticular density.
steps.normal: No erosions; no osteophytes or periostitis; normal bone mineralisation.
findings: Marginal erosions at the [ ] with periarticular osteopenia, favouring rheumatoid arthritis.
Central "gull-wing" erosions of the [DIP / PIP] joints, compatible with erosive osteoarthritis.
Erosions with fluffy periostitis and new bone formation (productive change), favouring psoriatic arthritis.
Well-defined punched-out erosions with overhanging edges and soft-tissue tophi, favouring gout.
steps.tip: Gout preserves mineralisation and joint space until late; rheumatoid arthritis causes periarticular osteopenia early.

steps.label: Alignment
steps.detail: Look for subluxation, ulnar deviation, swan-neck or boutonnière deformity, carpal collapse and ankylosis.
steps.look: PA and oblique hand views; lateral cervical flexion and extension views when atlanto-axial involvement is in question.
steps.normal: Normal alignment without subluxation or deformity.
findings: Ulnar deviation and volar subluxation at the MCP joints.
Carpal collapse with [scapholunate dissociation / ulnar translocation of the carpus].
Atlanto-dental interval of __ mm on flexion, compatible with atlanto-axial subluxation.
steps.tip: Deformity can be reducible; describe what the projection shows rather than inferring a fixed deformity.

steps.label: Soft tissues, calcification and change
steps.detail: Describe swelling, tophi, chondrocalcinosis or other calcification, and interval structural progression.
steps.look: Soft tissues around each joint; the triangular fibrocartilage and hyaline cartilage for chondrocalcinosis; direct comparison with the prior study.
steps.normal: No soft-tissue swelling, calcification or tophi; no interval progression.
findings: Chondrocalcinosis of the triangular fibrocartilage, compatible with CPPD deposition.
Eccentric dense soft-tissue masses compatible with tophi.
New erosions at the [ ] since [date], indicating progression.
Fusiform periarticular soft-tissue swelling of the [ ] joints.
steps.tip: Septic arthritis may be radiographically normal early; a single hot joint needs aspiration, not a pattern diagnosis.

steps.label: Location, age and margin
steps.detail: Name the bone, epiphysis, metaphysis or diaphysis, the central, eccentric, cortical or juxtacortical position, and the zone of transition, with the patient's age.
steps.look: Radiographs in two planes first: find the lesion's centre and inspect its whole margin, then correlate with CT or MRI.
steps.normal: No focal bone lesion in the imaged bones.
findings: Well-defined lytic lesion with a narrow zone of transition and sclerotic margin in the eccentric metaphysis of the [bone] (non-aggressive pattern).
Ill-defined permeative or moth-eaten lesion with a wide zone of transition in the diaphysis of the [bone] (aggressive pattern).
Epiphyseal lesion in a skeletally [immature / mature] patient, __ mm.
steps.tip: Age and the zone of transition are the two most informative features; a wide transition zone indicates aggressive behaviour but not a specific diagnosis.

steps.label: Matrix, periosteum and cortex
steps.detail: Describe matrix mineralisation, periosteal reaction, cortical thinning, scalloping or breach, and any pathological fracture.
steps.look: Radiographs and CT bone window for matrix and cortex; inspect the periosteal surface along the full length of the lesion.
findings: Chondroid matrix with rings-and-arcs calcification.
Cloud-like osteoid matrix [with / without] sunburst periosteal reaction and a Codman triangle.
Solid, uninterrupted periosteal reaction, favouring a slow-growing process.
Lamellated periosteal reaction with cortical breach.
steps.tip: Solid periosteal new bone suggests slow growth; interrupted, lamellated or sunburst reactions suggest an aggressive process.

steps.label: Local extent and size
steps.detail: Measure the intramedullary lesion and any extraosseous component separately in three planes.
steps.look: MRI T1 for marrow extent against normal fatty marrow and fluid-sensitive images for the soft-tissue component; image the whole bone when sarcoma is suspected.
findings: Intramedullary lesion measuring __ × __ × __ mm (series __ image __).
Extraosseous soft-tissue component measuring __ × __ × __ mm.
Peritumoral oedema extending __ cm beyond the lesion margin.
steps.tip: Measure tumour extent on T1; oedema on fluid-sensitive images overstates it.

steps.label: Joint, physis and neurovascular relationships
steps.detail: State physeal or articular involvement, compartments, and the relationship to the neurovascular bundle.
steps.look: Axial MRI through the soft-tissue component for the neurovascular bundle; coronal and sagittal images for the physis and joint.
findings: Tumour crosses the physis into the epiphysis; no intra-articular extension.
Soft-tissue component abuts the neurovascular bundle over less than half its circumference, without encasement.
Extension into the [ ] compartment / joint.

steps.label: Multiplicity and comparison
steps.detail: Look for further or skip lesions and compare with prior imaging for growth.
steps.look: The whole imaged bone and every included bone; prior radiographs for change in size or margin.
findings: Solitary lesion; no skip lesion in the imaged bone.
Multiple lesions in [ ]; metastases, myeloma or a polyostotic benign process according to age.
Unchanged since [date], supporting a non-aggressive lesion.
steps.tip: In a patient over 40, consider metastasis and myeloma for any lytic lesion.

steps.label: Site and matrix
steps.detail: Name the bone, central or surface location and the chondroid rings-and-arcs matrix.
steps.look: Radiographs of the whole bone and CT for rings-and-arcs calcification; decide whether the lesion is central or a surface lesion.
findings: Central chondroid lesion in the [metaphysis / diaphysis] of the [bone] with rings-and-arcs calcification, __ mm.
[Sessile / pedunculated] osteochondroma of the [bone] with cortical and medullary continuity.
Chondroid lesion of the [pelvis / scapula / rib] (axial location).
steps.tip: Location matters: a chondroid lesion of the pelvis, shoulder girdle or axial skeleton is more often malignant than one in the hands or feet.

steps.label: Endosteal and cortical change
steps.detail: Describe endosteal scalloping depth and length, cortical thickening, expansion, breach and periosteal reaction.
steps.look: CT or radiographs perpendicular to the cortex along the full length of the lesion.
steps.normal: No endosteal scalloping, cortical change or periosteal reaction.
findings: Endosteal scalloping of about __% of cortical thickness over __ mm, without cortical breach.
Deep endosteal scalloping (more than two-thirds of the cortical thickness) with cortical thickening and expansion.
Cortical breach with periosteal reaction.
steps.tip: Cortical thickening and expansion are signs of an active lesion even without a breach.

steps.label: MRI characteristics
steps.detail: Assess lobulated cartilage signal, entrapped fat, peritumoral oedema and enhancement pattern.
steps.look: T1 for marrow extent and entrapped fat; fat-suppressed T2 for lobulation and oedema; post-contrast (dynamic when acquired) for enhancement.
findings: Lobulated T2-hyperintense lesion with entrapped fat and peripheral septal enhancement; no peritumoral oedema.
Peritumoral marrow oedema and [early arterial / nodular] enhancement.
Loss of the lobular pattern with a T1-hypointense non-chondroid component, raising concern for dedifferentiation.
steps.tip: Preserved entrapped marrow fat favours a low-grade lesion; loss of the lobular pattern or a non-chondroid component raises concern for higher grade.

steps.label: Soft tissue and cartilage cap
steps.detail: Look for a soft-tissue mass; for an osteochondroma confirm continuity and measure the cartilage cap.
steps.look: MRI or ultrasound perpendicular to the underlying bone at the thickest part of the cap; surrounding soft tissues.
steps.normal: No soft-tissue mass.
findings: Cartilage cap __ mm at its thickest point.
Cartilage cap thicker than 1.5–2 cm in a skeletally mature patient, raising concern for secondary chondrosarcoma.
Soft-tissue mass __ × __ mm extending from the lesion.
Bursa overlying the osteochondroma, __ mm.
steps.tip: Cap thickness is only reassuring after skeletal maturity; caps are normally thicker in growing children.

steps.label: Growth and grade-relevant features
steps.detail: Compare with prior imaging and summarise the features that favour enchondroma, atypical cartilaginous tumour or higher-grade chondrosarcoma.
steps.look: Prior radiographs and MRI of the same region, measured like for like.
findings: No interval growth since [date]; features favour enchondroma.
Features favour an atypical cartilaginous tumour: [list].
Growth after skeletal maturity since [date]; specialist bone-tumour review is warranted.
steps.tip: Growth of a chondroid lesion or an osteochondroma after skeletal maturity warrants specialist review.

steps.label: Malleolar fractures
steps.detail: Locate the fibular fracture relative to the syndesmosis and assess the medial and posterior malleoli.
steps.look: Mortise and lateral views: lateral malleolus, medial malleolus, then the posterior tibial lip.
steps.normal: No malleolar fracture.
findings: Weber [A / B / C] fibular fracture, displaced __ mm.
Medial malleolar fracture, [transverse / vertical].
Posterior malleolar fracture involving about __% of the articular surface.

steps.label: Mortise and syndesmosis
steps.detail: Check talar centring, medial clear space and the distal tibiofibular relationship.
steps.look: True mortise view; compare the medial and superior clear spaces; include the proximal fibula when the pattern requires it.
steps.normal: Mortise congruent; medial clear space normal; distal tibiofibular relationship normal.
findings: Medial clear space widened to __ mm with lateral talar shift.
Distal tibiofibular widening, compatible with syndesmotic injury.
Proximal fibular fracture (Maisonneuve pattern).

steps.label: Talus, calcaneus and subtalar joint
steps.detail: Check the talar dome, lateral and posterior talar processes, calcaneus and subtalar joint.
steps.look: Lateral view and CT for the lateral talar process and anterior calcaneal process; Böhler angle for calcaneal compression.
steps.normal: Talar dome, talar processes and calcaneus intact; subtalar joint congruent.
findings: Fracture of the lateral process of the talus.
Fracture of the anterior process of the calcaneus at the calcaneocuboid joint.
Calcaneal fracture with a reduced Böhler angle of __° and subtalar joint involvement.
Osteochondral lesion of the talar dome, __ mm.
steps.tip: Lateral talar process and anterior calcaneal process fractures mimic an ankle sprain clinically and are easily missed on radiographs.

steps.label: Midfoot and forefoot
steps.detail: Check tarsometatarsal (Lisfranc) alignment, the navicular, the cuboid and the base of the fifth metatarsal.
steps.look: AP (weight-bearing when possible) and oblique views: the second metatarsal aligns with the intermediate cuneiform and the fourth metatarsal with the cuboid; CT for subtle injury.
steps.normal: Tarsometatarsal alignment normal; no midfoot or metatarsal fracture.
findings: Lisfranc injury: __ mm widening between the first and second metatarsal bases with a fleck fragment and lateral subluxation of the second metatarsal.
Fracture of the base of the fifth metatarsal: [tuberosity avulsion / metaphyseal–diaphyseal junction (Jones) fracture].
Navicular [body / dorsal avulsion] fracture.
steps.tip: Subtle Lisfranc instability may appear only on weight-bearing views; a normal non-weight-bearing film does not exclude it.

steps.label: Ligaments and tendons
steps.detail: Name any ligament or tendon injury on MRI or ultrasound and distinguish partial from complete tears.
steps.look: MRI axial images tendon by tendon, ligament-specific planes, or targeted ultrasound.
steps.normal: No ligament or tendon injury on the examinations acquired.
findings: Complete tear of the anterior talofibular ligament.
Longitudinal split tear of peroneus brevis.
Lisfranc ligament [partial / complete] tear on MRI.

model.reporting_aim: Relate the ulcer to the underlying metatarsal heads, midfoot joints or calcaneus before describing marrow change.

steps.label: Ulcer and sinus tract
steps.detail: Find the skin defect (marker) and trace any tract through the soft tissues to bone or joint.
steps.look: T1 and fluid-sensitive images in two planes from the skin marker to the nearest bone; post-contrast images for the tract wall.
steps.normal: No skin ulcer or sinus tract; subcutaneous tissues unremarkable.
findings: Ulcer beneath the [first metatarsal head / fifth metatarsal head / heel] with a sinus tract extending to the [ ].
Ulcer with surrounding cellulitis; no tract to bone.
Soft-tissue defect in direct contact with the cortex of the [ ].
steps.tip: Osteomyelitis in the diabetic foot almost always spreads from an adjacent ulcer; marrow change far from any ulcer suggests another cause.

steps.label: Bone marrow
steps.detail: Separate confluent medullary T1 low signal (replacement of fatty marrow) from isolated fluid-sensitive oedema.
steps.look: T1 images first — confluent, medullary, geographic low signal is the key sign — then fluid-sensitive and post-contrast images for extent.
steps.normal: Normal marrow signal on T1 and fluid-sensitive sequences; no osteomyelitis.
findings: Confluent T1 hypointensity replacing fatty marrow in the [ ], contiguous with the ulcer tract, with corresponding fluid-sensitive signal and cortical destruction: osteomyelitis.
Fluid-sensitive marrow signal in the [ ] with preserved T1 fatty marrow: reactive osteitis rather than osteomyelitis.
Osteomyelitis extends __ mm from the [distal / proximal] end of the [ ].
steps.tip: Marrow oedema without T1 replacement of fatty marrow does not establish osteomyelitis.

steps.label: Joints and neuroarthropathy
steps.detail: Describe joint-centred distribution, subchondral oedema, fragmentation, subluxation and deformity.
steps.look: Sagittal and axial images of the Lisfranc and Chopart joints; compare the location with the ulcer.
steps.normal: No neuropathic arthropathy; joint alignment normal.
findings: Acute Charcot neuroarthropathy of the [Lisfranc / Chopart] joints: periarticular subchondral marrow oedema centred on the joints, without an ulcer or tract.
Chronic Charcot foot with fragmentation, subluxation and rocker-bottom deformity.
Charcot joint with an adjacent ulcer, tract and diffuse T1 marrow replacement: superimposed osteomyelitis is likely.
steps.tip: Neuroarthropathy is joint-centred and midfoot-predominant; infection is ulcer-centred at pressure points. Bone margins that fade on T1 but reappear after contrast (the ghost sign) favour infection.

steps.label: Abscess and devitalised tissue
steps.detail: Look for fluid collections with rim enhancement, gas and non-enhancing (devitalised) tissue.
steps.look: Fluid-sensitive and post-contrast fat-suppressed images; gas appears as signal void on all sequences.
steps.normal: No abscess, gas or devitalised tissue.
findings: Rim-enhancing collection in the [medial / central / lateral plantar / dorsal] compartment measuring __ × __ × __ mm.
Non-enhancing soft tissue at the [ ], compatible with devitalised tissue.
Soft-tissue gas along the [ ].
steps.tip: Without contrast, a collection and devitalised tissue cannot be separated reliably; state this limitation.

steps.label: Tendons, compartments and postoperative changes
steps.detail: Review tenosynovitis, tendon continuity, spread through the plantar compartments and any amputation stump.
steps.look: Axial images along the flexor and extensor tendon sheaths and the plantar compartments.
steps.normal: Tendons intact without tenosynovitis; no spread along the plantar compartments.
findings: Septic tenosynovitis of the [flexor hallucis longus] sheath extending proximally to [ ].
Infection spreading through the [medial / central / lateral] plantar compartment.
Amputation stump of the [ ] with [no / new] marrow signal change at the resection margin.

steps.label: Tendons
steps.detail: Assess the common extensor and flexor origins, the distal biceps at the radial tuberosity and the triceps at the olecranon.
steps.look: Coronal images for the common extensor and flexor origins; axial and sagittal images for the distal biceps; sagittal images for the triceps.
steps.normal: Common extensor and flexor origins, distal biceps and triceps tendons intact with normal signal.
findings: Common extensor origin tendinosis with [partial-thickness / high-grade partial / full-thickness] tear, __ mm (lateral epicondylitis).
Complete distal biceps tendon rupture retracted __ mm [with / without] an intact lacertus fibrosus.
Partial distal biceps tear with radiobicipital bursitis.
Common flexor origin tendinosis (medial epicondylitis).
steps.tip: Lateral epicondylitis can coexist with a tear of the lateral ulnar collateral ligament beneath the extensor origin; look deep to the tendon.

steps.label: Collateral ligaments
steps.detail: Name the ulnar collateral ligament (anterior bundle) and lateral collateral complex components and any tear site.
steps.look: Coronal images for the anterior bundle of the UCL to the sublime tubercle and for the lateral ulnar collateral ligament behind the radial head; axial images for the annular ligament.
steps.normal: Ulnar collateral ligament and lateral collateral ligament complex intact.
findings: Tear of the anterior bundle of the UCL at its [humeral / sublime tubercle] attachment.
Undersurface partial tear of the distal UCL with fluid tracking along the sublime tubercle (T-sign).
Lateral ulnar collateral ligament tear, compatible with posterolateral rotatory instability in the appropriate clinical setting.
Avulsion fracture of the sublime tubercle.

steps.label: Cartilage and bone
steps.detail: Inspect capitellar and trochlear cartilage, osteochondral lesions, marrow and fracture.
steps.look: Sagittal and coronal images of the capitellum and trochlea; T1 for fracture lines.
steps.normal: Articular cartilage preserved; no osteochondral lesion, marrow oedema or fracture.
findings: Osteochondral lesion of the capitellum, __ × __ × __ mm, [stable / with fluid undercutting the fragment].
Occult radial head fracture with marrow oedema.
Posteromedial olecranon osteophytes (valgus extension overload).
steps.tip: The pseudodefect of the capitellum lies posterolaterally at the junction with the lateral epicondyle and must not be called an osteochondral lesion.

steps.label: Nerves and muscles
steps.detail: Trace the ulnar nerve through the cubital tunnel, the radial nerve and posterior interosseous nerve at the supinator, and the median nerve; look for denervation.
steps.look: Axial images from above the elbow into the proximal forearm, following each nerve.
steps.normal: Ulnar, radial and median nerves normal in calibre and signal; no denervation oedema.
findings: Ulnar nerve enlargement and increased signal in the cubital tunnel [with an anconeus epitrochlearis / osteophytes].
Denervation oedema of the supinator and extensor muscles, compatible with posterior interosseous neuropathy.
Compressing lesion [ ] along the [ ] nerve.
steps.tip: Mildly increased ulnar nerve signal is common in asymptomatic elbows; enlargement and denervation are more specific.

steps.label: Joint, recesses and loose bodies
steps.detail: Review alignment, effusion, synovitis, loose bodies, synovial folds and postoperative change.
steps.look: Sagittal images of the anterior and posterior recesses and olecranon fossa; coronal images for a lateral synovial fold.
steps.normal: Normal alignment; no effusion, synovitis or loose bodies.
findings: Joint effusion with [number] intra-articular loose bodies in the [olecranon / coronoid] fossa.
Thickened lateral synovial fold [with adjacent chondral change].
Postoperative change after [UCL reconstruction / tendon repair] with [intact / failed] repair.
steps.tip: Synovial folds and accessory ossicles can mimic loose bodies; confirm on two planes.

model.reporting_aim: Relate the capitellum, radial head and olecranon to the distal humerus before checking the alignment lines.

steps.label: Fat pads and effusion
steps.detail: Look for a visible posterior fat pad or an elevated anterior fat pad as signs of a joint effusion.
steps.look: True lateral in 90 degrees of flexion: anterior fat pad over the coronoid fossa, posterior fat pad in the olecranon fossa.
steps.normal: Anterior fat pad normal; posterior fat pad not visible; no effusion.
findings: Elevated anterior fat pad ("sail sign") and a visible posterior fat pad: joint effusion.
Joint effusion without a visible fracture; an occult fracture is possible, most often supracondylar.
steps.tip: On a true lateral in flexion, a visible posterior fat pad is always abnormal.

steps.label: Alignment lines
steps.detail: Check the anterior humeral line on the true lateral and the radiocapitellar line on every view.
steps.look: True lateral: the anterior humeral line should cross the middle third of the capitellum. Every view: the radiocapitellar line should pass through the capitellum.
steps.normal: Anterior humeral line passes through the middle third of the capitellum; the radiocapitellar line is aligned on all views.
findings: Anterior humeral line passes anterior to the middle third of the capitellum: posterior displacement of the capitellum (extension-type supracondylar fracture).
Radiocapitellar line misses the capitellum: radial head dislocation; examine the ulna for a Monteggia fracture.
steps.tip: In very young children with a small capitellum the anterior humeral line may pass through its anterior third; use age and a true lateral before calling displacement.

steps.label: Ossification centres (CRITOE)
steps.detail: Match the visible centres to age in the order capitellum, radial head, internal (medial) epicondyle, trochlea, olecranon, external (lateral) epicondyle.
steps.look: AP and lateral: count the centres and confirm the medial epicondyle sits at the medial humerus, not in the joint.
steps.normal: Ossification centres appropriate for age and normally positioned.
findings: Medial epicondyle ossification centre displaced __ mm [distally / into the joint].
Ossicle in the trochlear position without a normally placed medial epicondyle: entrapped medial epicondyle.
Lateral condyle fragment displaced __ mm.
steps.tip: The centres appear at roughly 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 and 11 years (earlier in girls); the trochlea does not ossify before the medial epicondyle.

steps.label: Fracture
steps.detail: Name the fracture — supracondylar, lateral condyle, medial epicondyle, radial head or neck, olecranon — and describe displacement.
steps.look: Both views: supracondylar region and posterior cortex on the lateral, lateral condyle on AP and oblique, radial neck and olecranon.
steps.normal: No fracture.
findings: Extension-type supracondylar fracture, Gartland type [I / II / III], with [posterior displacement / rotation].
Lateral condyle fracture displaced __ mm.
Radial neck fracture with __° angulation.
Medial epicondyle avulsion displaced __ mm.
steps.tip: Lateral condyle fractures can be subtle on the AP view; displacement of 2 mm or more usually changes management.

steps.label: Forearm and associated injury
steps.detail: Look for a forearm fracture with radial head dislocation, a second fracture and post-reduction alignment.
steps.look: Include the forearm when the radiocapitellar line is disrupted: look for ulnar fracture or plastic bowing.
steps.normal: No forearm fracture or radial head dislocation.
findings: Monteggia fracture-dislocation: ulnar [fracture / plastic bowing] with anterior radial head dislocation.
Elbow dislocation [posterolateral] [with / without] medial epicondyle avulsion.
Post-reduction alignment [satisfactory / persistent displacement].

steps.label: Component position
steps.detail: Measure cup inclination and describe cup and stem position, migration and subsidence against the earliest postoperative film.
steps.look: AP pelvis centred on the symphysis: cup inclination against the inter-teardrop line and leg length; lateral view for version; stem position against the greater trochanter on the first postoperative film.
steps.normal: Components in satisfactory position, unchanged from [date]; no migration or subsidence.
findings: Acetabular cup inclination __° relative to the inter-teardrop line.
Femoral stem subsidence of __ mm since [date].
Cup migration [medial / superior] with change in inclination since [date].
steps.tip: Compare only comparable projections; pelvic tilt and rotation alter apparent cup inclination and version.

steps.label: Bone–implant interfaces
steps.detail: Map lucent lines and osteolysis by acetabular (DeLee–Charnley) and femoral (Gruen) zones and compare with prior films.
steps.look: AP and lateral views: acetabular zones 1–3 and femoral zones 1–7 on AP and 8–14 on the lateral.
steps.normal: No periprosthetic lucency or osteolysis.
findings: Thin, non-progressive lucent line (under 2 mm) in Gruen zone __, unchanged.
Progressive lucency of __ mm in Gruen zones __, compatible with loosening.
Focal scalloped osteolysis in DeLee–Charnley zone __ measuring __ mm, compatible with particle disease.
steps.tip: A lucency wider than 2 mm, progressive widening or a circumferential lucency suggests loosening; a thin stable line can be normal.

steps.label: Bearing surface and hardware
steps.detail: Look for eccentric femoral head position (liner wear), cement mantle defects and broken components.
steps.look: AP pelvis: femoral head centre relative to the cup centre; cement mantle; screws, wires and stem.
steps.normal: Femoral head concentric within the cup; cement mantle intact; no hardware fracture.
findings: Eccentric superolateral position of the femoral head within the cup, compatible with polyethylene wear.
Fracture of the [stem / cement mantle / screw].
Dissociation of the acetabular liner.

steps.label: Bone stock, fracture and dislocation
steps.detail: Assess periprosthetic fracture, bone stock, dislocation and heterotopic ossification.
steps.look: The full length of the stem to its tip and the whole acetabulum; the periprosthetic cortex.
steps.normal: No periprosthetic fracture or dislocation; no heterotopic ossification.
findings: Periprosthetic femoral fracture [around / below] the stem tip with a [loose / well-fixed] stem.
Posterior dislocation of the femoral head component.
Heterotopic ossification [Brooker class __ / described].
steps.tip: The film must include the whole stem tip, where periprosthetic fractures commonly occur.

steps.label: Soft tissues and comparison
steps.detail: Describe soft-tissue findings, periosteal reaction and interval change, and whether the pattern warrants an infection work-up.
steps.look: Soft tissues about the hip and comparison with every available prior film.
steps.normal: Soft tissues unremarkable; no interval change since [date].
findings: Periosteal reaction and rapidly progressive lucency since [date]; infection should be considered and aspiration may be required.
Soft-tissue mass adjacent to the prosthesis; an adverse local tissue reaction should be assessed with ultrasound or MRI.
steps.tip: Infection and aseptic loosening can look identical on radiographs; rapid progression and periosteal reaction raise concern for infection.

steps.label: Femoral head–neck morphology
steps.detail: Assess head–neck sphericity and cam morphology at the anterosuperior head–neck junction.
steps.look: Dunn (45 degree) or cross-table lateral view, and radial MRI reformats at the anterosuperior (about 1–2 o'clock) head–neck junction.
steps.normal: Normal femoral head–neck offset without cam morphology.
findings: Cam morphology: osseous bump at the anterosuperior head–neck junction; alpha angle __° on the [Dunn view / radial MRI at __ o'clock].
Reduced femoral head–neck offset without a discrete bump.
Herniation pit at the anterior femoral neck.
steps.tip: The alpha angle depends on projection and clock-face position; always state where it was measured.

steps.label: Acetabular coverage and version
steps.detail: Measure the lateral centre-edge angle and look for crossover, posterior wall and ischial spine signs, coxa profunda or protrusio.
steps.look: A well-centred AP pelvis with the coccyx over the symphysis, 1–3 cm above it.
steps.normal: Normal lateral acetabular coverage; no crossover sign, dysplasia or protrusio.
findings: Pincer morphology: lateral centre-edge angle __° [with coxa profunda / protrusio].
Crossover and posterior wall signs indicating acetabular retroversion.
Undercoverage: lateral centre-edge angle __°, compatible with acetabular dysplasia.
steps.tip: Pelvic tilt and rotation create false crossover signs; check the coccyx–symphysis relationship first.

steps.label: Labrum (if MRI acquired)
steps.detail: If MRI or MR arthrography was acquired, localise tearing, detachment and paralabral cysts; otherwise state that the labrum is not assessed.
steps.look: Radial or oblique small-field MRI (MR arthrography when performed) around the acetabular clock face.
steps.normal: Acetabular labrum intact without tear, detachment or paralabral cyst.
findings: Labrum not assessed: no MRI acquired.
Anterosuperior labral tear from __ to __ o'clock [with / without] chondrolabral detachment.
Paralabral cyst __ mm adjacent to the [ ] labrum.
steps.tip: Labral tears in femoroacetabular impingement are usually anterosuperior; relate them to the site of the cam or pincer morphology.

steps.label: Joint space and cartilage
steps.detail: Describe radiographic joint-space loss and subchondral change; map cartilage lesions only if MRI was acquired.
steps.look: AP pelvis for joint space; MRI proton-density or fluid-sensitive images for acetabular and femoral cartilage.
steps.normal: Joint space preserved; no subchondral sclerosis or cysts; cartilage intact where assessed.
findings: Superolateral joint-space narrowing to __ mm with subchondral cysts: secondary osteoarthritis.
Anterosuperior acetabular chondral delamination adjacent to the cam morphology (MRI).
Focal chondral defect of the [femoral head / acetabulum], __ × __ mm.
steps.tip: Established osteoarthritis changes the treatment discussion; report joint-space width even when morphology is the question.

steps.label: Alternative pain generators
steps.detail: Assess periarticular tendons, bursae, muscles and the visible pelvic structures.
steps.look: The whole AP pelvis — sacroiliac joints, pubic symphysis, anterior inferior iliac spine — and MRI of periarticular tendons and bursae when acquired.
steps.normal: No alternative pain generator identified.
findings: Prominent anterior inferior iliac spine extending to the acetabular rim (subspine impingement morphology).
Gluteus [medius / minimus] tendinopathy [with partial tear] at the greater trochanter.
Femoral head subchondral fracture or osteonecrosis.

steps.label: Menisci
steps.detail: Inspect both menisci — anterior horn, body, posterior horn and roots — for tear, displaced fragment and extrusion.
steps.look: Sagittal proton-density images through each meniscus from periphery to root; coronal images for the body, roots and extrusion; search the notch for displaced fragments.
steps.normal: Medial and lateral menisci intact, including the roots; no extrusion or displaced fragment.
findings: [Horizontal / oblique / longitudinal / radial] tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus extending to the [inferior] articular surface.
Bucket-handle tear of the [medial] meniscus with a fragment displaced into the intercondylar notch (double PCL sign).
Posterior root tear of the [medial] meniscus with __ mm extrusion.
Fragment of the [lateral] meniscus flipped into the anterior horn region.
steps.tip: Call a tear only when abnormal signal reaches an articular surface on at least two images, or when the meniscal shape is abnormal.

steps.label: Cruciate and collateral ligaments
steps.detail: Assess the ACL, PCL, MCL and posterolateral corner for continuity, tear site and associated avulsion.
steps.look: Sagittal images for the cruciates; coronal images for the collateral ligaments and posterolateral corner (biceps femoris, popliteus); axial images through the posterolateral corner.
steps.normal: Cruciate and collateral ligaments and posterolateral corner structures intact.
findings: Complete ACL tear with bone contusions of the lateral femoral condyle and posterolateral tibial plateau (pivot-shift pattern).
Segond fracture: avulsion from the lateral tibial rim, associated with ACL tear.
MCL injury: [periligamentous oedema / partial tear / complete tear] at the [femoral / tibial] attachment.
Posterolateral corner injury involving the [LCL / biceps femoris / popliteus tendon]; fibular head avulsion.
steps.tip: Posterolateral corner injuries are easily overlooked alongside an ACL tear but change surgical planning.

steps.label: Cartilage and subchondral bone
steps.detail: Map chondral loss, osteochondral lesions, contusions and subchondral fracture by compartment.
steps.look: Fluid-sensitive images in all planes for chondral defects and contusions; T1 for fracture lines.
steps.normal: Articular cartilage preserved; no contusion, subchondral fracture or osteochondral lesion.
findings: Full-thickness chondral defect of the [medial femoral condyle], __ × __ mm.
Subchondral insufficiency fracture of the [medial femoral condyle] with marrow oedema.
Osteochondritis dissecans of the [lateral aspect of the medial femoral condyle] with fluid undercutting the fragment (unstable).
steps.tip: A fluid-bright line or cysts beneath an osteochondral fragment indicate instability.

steps.label: Extensor mechanism and patellofemoral joint
steps.detail: Review the quadriceps and patellar tendons, patellar position, medial patellofemoral ligament and trochlea.
steps.look: Sagittal images for the tendons; axial images for patellar position, the medial patellofemoral ligament and trochlear shape.
steps.normal: Quadriceps and patellar tendons intact; patella centred; medial patellofemoral ligament and retinacula intact; normal trochlea.
findings: Transient lateral patellar dislocation: medial patellofemoral ligament tear at the [femoral / patellar] attachment with medial patellar and lateral femoral condyle contusions.
Patellar tendinopathy at the inferior patellar pole.
Complete quadriceps tendon rupture with a __ mm gap.
Trochlear dysplasia with a [shallow / flat] trochlea.
steps.tip: The contusion pattern of patellar dislocation (medial patella and lateral femoral condyle) persists after spontaneous reduction.

steps.label: Joint and posterior structures
steps.detail: Assess effusion, synovitis, loose bodies, popliteal cyst, posteromedial structures and postoperative change.
steps.look: Axial and sagittal images of the suprapatellar recess, Hoffa fat pad, popliteal fossa and posteromedial corner.
steps.normal: No significant effusion, synovitis or loose bodies; no popliteal cyst.
findings: Moderate joint effusion with [number] loose bodies.
Popliteal cyst __ × __ mm between the medial gastrocnemius and semimembranosus [with rupture and fluid tracking distally].
Parameniscal cyst adjacent to a [horizontal] tear of the [ ] meniscus.
steps.tip: A popliteal cyst arises between the medial gastrocnemius and semimembranosus; a collection elsewhere needs another explanation.

steps.label: Injured muscle–tendon unit
steps.detail: Name the muscle, side and compartment, and whether the injury is myofascial, myotendinous or intratendinous.
steps.look: Axial fluid-sensitive images to identify the muscle; coronal or sagittal images for the level along the unit.
steps.normal: Normal muscle signal and architecture; no muscle injury.
findings: Myotendinous junction injury of the [ ] at the [proximal / mid / distal] third.
Myofascial (peripheral) injury of the [ ] with fluid along the epimysium.
Intratendinous injury of the central tendon of the [rectus femoris].
steps.tip: Name the muscle and the site along the unit; myofascial, myotendinous and intratendinous injuries recover differently.

steps.label: Fibre disruption
steps.detail: Separate oedema with preserved architecture from partial or complete structural disruption.
steps.look: Axial and longitudinal fluid-sensitive images for loss of the normal feathery fibre pattern and discontinuity.
steps.normal: Muscle architecture preserved.
findings: Oedema with preserved architecture (low-grade strain).
Partial fibre disruption involving approximately __% of the cross-sectional area.
Complete disruption with a __ mm gap and retraction.

steps.label: Tendon and aponeurosis
steps.detail: Assess the central tendon, aponeurosis and origin or insertion.
steps.look: Longitudinal images along the intramuscular tendon and aponeurosis to its attachment.
steps.normal: Central tendon, aponeurosis and attachments intact.
findings: Central tendon disruption of the [ ] (intratendinous extension).
Avulsion of the [ ] tendon from its [origin / insertion] [with / without] a bone fragment.
steps.tip: Extension into the intramuscular tendon is associated with longer recovery than a purely myofascial injury.

steps.label: Oedema and haematoma
steps.detail: Describe the extent of oedema and the site and size of any haematoma.
steps.look: Fluid-sensitive images for craniocaudal oedema length; T1 and fluid-sensitive images for haematoma signal.
steps.normal: No oedema or haematoma.
findings: Oedema extends __ cm craniocaudally, involving about __% of the maximal cross-sectional area.
Intramuscular haematoma __ × __ × __ mm.
Closed degloving (Morel-Lavallée) collection between the subcutaneous fat and fascia over the [ ], __ mm.

steps.label: Associated findings
steps.detail: Look for nerve proximity, bone contusion, scar from earlier injury and alternative explanations.
steps.look: Adjacent nerves, bone and fascia; comparison with earlier injuries at the same site.
steps.normal: No associated nerve, bone or fascial abnormality.
findings: Scar from previous injury at the [ ] with new adjacent oedema (re-injury).
Peripheral mineralisation within the haematoma on radiograph or CT, compatible with myositis ossificans.
Haematoma displaces the [sciatic] nerve without nerve signal change.
steps.tip: Early myositis ossificans can mimic a soft-tissue sarcoma on MRI; radiographs or CT show its peripheral mineralisation.

steps.label: Distribution
steps.detail: Map the involved muscles and whether the change follows a nerve, a compartment or a systemic pattern.
steps.look: Bilateral axial T1 and fluid-sensitive images of the symptomatic region, muscle by muscle.
steps.normal: Normal bulk and signal of all imaged muscles, symmetric.
findings: Symmetric proximal muscle oedema involving [ ] with relative sparing of [ ], compatible with an inflammatory myopathy in the appropriate clinical setting.
Change confined to the muscles supplied by the [ ] nerve, favouring denervation.
Selective involvement of [ ] with sparing of [ ], a pattern that may suggest [a specific myopathy].
steps.tip: A distribution needs both sides; unilateral coverage can miss symmetric disease.

steps.label: Oedema
steps.detail: Describe fluid-sensitive signal, focal or diffuse involvement, and fascial and subcutaneous change.
steps.look: Fat-suppressed fluid-sensitive axial images; note fascial and subcutaneous involvement.
steps.normal: No muscle, fascial or subcutaneous oedema.
findings: Diffuse muscle oedema in [ ] with perifascial fluid.
Thickening and fluid along the deep fascia [with gas]; in the appropriate clinical context this raises concern for necrotising fasciitis.
Patchy intramuscular oedema without fascial involvement.
steps.tip: Muscle oedema is non-specific: inflammation, denervation, exertion, radiation and infection can all cause it.

steps.label: Fatty change and atrophy
steps.detail: Use T1 images to separate chronic fatty replacement from active oedema.
steps.look: Axial T1 images for fatty streaks and volume loss; compare sides.
steps.normal: No fatty replacement or atrophy.
findings: Fatty replacement of [ ], [mild / moderate / severe], with volume loss.
Mixed pattern: fatty replacement with active oedema in [ ].
Unilateral fatty atrophy of the [ ] in the [ ] nerve territory (chronic denervation).
steps.tip: Acute denervation causes oedema within weeks; fatty atrophy takes months.

steps.label: Collection or mass
steps.detail: Identify focal lesions, abscess, blood products and enhancement if acquired.
steps.look: Fluid-sensitive and contrast-enhanced images; diffusion if acquired.
steps.normal: No intramuscular collection or mass.
findings: Intramuscular abscess (pyomyositis) in the [ ] measuring __ × __ × __ mm with rim enhancement.
Focal intramuscular mass __ mm that needs dedicated mass characterisation.

steps.label: Nerves and associated structures
steps.detail: Inspect visible nerves, entrapment sites, tendons, bone and accessory muscles for a cause.
steps.look: Axial images along the nerves that supply the involved muscles, including known entrapment sites.
steps.normal: No nerve abnormality, entrapment lesion or accessory muscle.
findings: Ganglion cyst at the [ ] compressing the [ ] nerve, with denervation of [ ].
Accessory muscle: [ ].
Tendon rupture explaining the muscle atrophy: [ ].

steps.label: Tendon identity
steps.detail: Identify the semimembranosus and the conjoint (semitendinosus and biceps femoris long head) origins separately at the ischial tuberosity.
steps.look: Axial images at the ischial tuberosity — semimembranosus anterolateral, conjoint tendon posteromedial — then follow each distally.
steps.normal: Semimembranosus and conjoint tendon origins intact; hamstring muscles normal.
findings: Injury of the biceps femoris long head at the proximal myotendinous junction.
Semimembranosus origin injury with an intact conjoint tendon.
Both the conjoint tendon and semimembranosus origins involved.
steps.tip: The biceps femoris long head is the most frequently injured hamstring; name each involved component.

steps.label: Tear type and location
steps.detail: Assess partial origin injury, full-thickness avulsion and myotendinous injury.
steps.look: Coronal and axial fluid-sensitive images of the free tendon, myotendinous junction and muscle belly.
steps.normal: No hamstring tear.
findings: Partial tear of the conjoint tendon origin involving about __% of the footprint, with residual attached fibres.
Complete avulsion of the [conjoint tendon / all three tendons] from the ischial tuberosity.
Intratendinous injury extending __ cm along the free tendon (British Athletics grade __c).

steps.label: Retraction
steps.detail: Measure each avulsed tendon from its footprint and describe the distal stump.
steps.look: Coronal images along the tendon from the ischial footprint to the stump; confirm on sagittal images.
steps.normal: No tendon retraction.
findings: Conjoint tendon retracted __ cm from the ischial tuberosity (coronal measurement).
Apophyseal avulsion fragment displaced __ mm.
steps.tip: Measure retraction along the tendon course on coronal images; axial images underestimate it.

steps.label: Muscle and haematoma
steps.detail: Map muscle oedema, structural fibre loss and haematoma.
steps.look: Axial and coronal fluid-sensitive images along the hamstring muscles.
steps.normal: No muscle oedema or haematoma.
findings: Muscle oedema extending __ cm craniocaudally.
Haematoma __ × __ × __ mm around the retracted tendon.
Retracted muscle belly bunched distally ("dropped ice cream" appearance).

steps.label: Sciatic nerve and associated findings
steps.detail: Assess the sciatic nerve relationship and adjacent bone or soft-tissue change.
steps.look: Axial images following the sciatic nerve lateral to the ischial tuberosity into the proximal thigh.
steps.normal: Sciatic nerve normal in course and signal; ischial tuberosity normal.
findings: Haematoma abuts and displaces the sciatic nerve without nerve signal change.
Sciatic nerve thickening and increased signal adjacent to [scar / haematoma].
Ischial tuberosity marrow oedema.

steps.label: Long head of biceps
steps.detail: Follow the tendon in the groove and rotator interval and assess stability during rotation.
steps.look: Transverse and longitudinal scans in the bicipital groove with the arm externally rotated; follow into the rotator interval; dynamic internal and external rotation.
steps.normal: Long-head biceps tendon in the groove with a normal fibrillar pattern; no sheath effusion; stable on dynamic rotation.
findings: Long-head biceps tendon absent from the groove, [subluxed / dislocated] medially [superficial to / within] the subscapularis.
Thickened, hypoechoic long-head biceps tendon with sheath fluid and hyperaemia (tenosynovitis).
Empty groove: long-head biceps rupture.
steps.tip: Anisotropy makes a tendon falsely hypoechoic; angle the probe perpendicular to the fibres before calling tendinopathy.

steps.label: Rotator cuff
steps.detail: Assess the subscapularis, supraspinatus and infraspinatus and describe any tear surface, thickness and dimensions.
steps.look: Subscapularis in external rotation; supraspinatus in the modified Crass position in long and short axis; infraspinatus posteriorly.
steps.normal: Subscapularis, supraspinatus and infraspinatus tendons intact with normal thickness and echotexture; no calcification.
findings: Full-thickness supraspinatus tear __ × __ mm with loss of the convex bursal contour [and retraction].
Partial-thickness [articular-sided / bursal-sided] supraspinatus tear, __ mm.
Calcific deposit in the [supraspinatus], __ mm, [hard with acoustic shadowing / soft without shadowing].
Tendinosis: thickened hypoechoic supraspinatus without a defect.
steps.tip: A full-thickness tear extends from the bursal to the articular surface, often with a flattened bursal contour; confirm it in two planes.

steps.label: Bursa and dynamic assessment
steps.detail: Assess subacromial–subdeltoid bursal distension and tendon and bursal movement.
steps.look: Longitudinal images over the supraspinatus at rest and during active abduction.
steps.normal: Subacromial–subdeltoid bursa not distended; smooth gliding of the cuff beneath the acromion during abduction.
findings: Subacromial–subdeltoid bursal distension of __ mm [with Doppler hyperaemia].
Bursal fluid pooling at the acromial edge with painful abduction.
steps.tip: Report the observed dynamic finding and the pain it produced rather than "impingement" as a diagnosis.

steps.label: Glenohumeral recess and acromioclavicular joint
steps.detail: Review the accessible posterior joint recess and the acromioclavicular joint with focal symptom correlation.
steps.look: Posterior transverse scan of the glenohumeral recess; coronal scan over the acromioclavicular joint.
steps.normal: No glenohumeral effusion in the posterior recess; acromioclavicular joint unremarkable.
findings: Glenohumeral effusion of __ mm in the posterior recess.
Acromioclavicular joint capsular distension and osteophytes [with focal tenderness].
Cortical irregularity of the greater tuberosity.

steps.label: Muscles and limitations
steps.detail: Assess cuff muscle bulk and any paralabral cyst, and state the deep structures not reliably evaluated.
steps.look: Supraspinous and infraspinous fossae in short axis; spinoglenoid notch posteriorly.
steps.normal: Cuff muscle bulk and echogenicity normal; no paralabral cyst. The labrum and deep intra-articular structures are not assessed by ultrasound.
findings: Increased echogenicity and reduced bulk of the [supraspinatus / infraspinatus] (fatty atrophy).
Cyst at the spinoglenoid notch, __ mm; MRI would assess for a labral tear.
Examination limited by [restricted movement / body habitus].

steps.label: Level and alignment
steps.detail: Identify each injured level and describe kyphosis, translation or rotation.
steps.look: Sagittal CT reformats for alignment and kyphosis; count from a documented reference and correlate ribs and transverse processes.
steps.normal: Normal thoracolumbar alignment without kyphosis or translation.
findings: Fracture of [ ], counted from [ ].
Local kyphosis of __° at [ ] ([method]).
Translation of __ mm of [ ] on [ ] (translation or rotation injury).
steps.tip: Translation or rotation in any plane indicates a type C injury, whatever the vertebral body looks like.

steps.label: Fracture morphology
steps.detail: Classify the vertebral body injury as compression, split, incomplete or complete burst, and assess the posterior wall.
steps.look: Sagittal and axial CT: anterior column, each endplate and the posterior wall.
steps.normal: No vertebral body fracture.
findings: Wedge compression fracture of [ ] (AO A1) with __% anterior height loss; posterior wall intact.
Split fracture of [ ] (AO A2).
Incomplete burst fracture of [ ] (AO A3): one endplate and the posterior wall involved.
Complete burst fracture of [ ] (AO A4): both endplates and the posterior wall involved, with retropulsion.
steps.tip: Posterior wall involvement separates a burst fracture from a compression fracture; check it on axial and sagittal images.

steps.label: Posterior ligamentous complex
steps.detail: Assess interspinous widening, facet diastasis or dislocation, horizontal posterior element fractures and MRI ligament signal.
steps.look: CT for interspinous distance, facet alignment and posterior element fractures; MRI fluid-sensitive sagittal images for supraspinous and interspinous ligaments and ligamentum flavum.
steps.normal: Posterior ligamentous complex intact: no interspinous widening, facet malalignment or posterior element fracture.
findings: Interspinous widening and facet diastasis at [ ], compatible with posterior tension-band disruption (AO B2).
Horizontal fracture through the spinous process, laminae and pedicles (Chance-type, AO B1).
Anterior tension-band (hyperextension) injury with anterior disc space widening (AO B3).
MRI: disrupted supraspinous and interspinous ligaments with fluid signal.
steps.tip: A perched or jumped facet is a translation injury; do not classify it by vertebral body morphology alone.

steps.label: Canal and neural elements
steps.detail: Describe retropulsion, canal compromise, epidural haematoma and cord, conus or cauda equina findings.
steps.look: Axial CT at the level of maximal retropulsion; MRI sagittal T2 for the cord, conus and epidural space.
steps.normal: Spinal canal preserved; no retropulsion or epidural haematoma; cord and conus normal where imaged.
findings: Retropulsed fragment of __ mm narrowing the canal to __ mm.
Epidural haematoma from [ ] to [ ] with [cord / thecal sac] compression.
Cord or conus oedema at [ ].

steps.label: Classification and other injuries
steps.detail: Give the AO type and TLICS imaging components, and survey the whole imaged spine and paraspinal tissues.
steps.look: Summarise morphology and posterior ligamentous complex findings; review the full imaged spine for non-contiguous fractures.
steps.normal: No additional spinal fracture; no paraspinal or visceral injury in the field of view.
findings: AO Spine type [ ]; TLICS morphology [ ] and posterior ligamentous complex [intact / indeterminate / disrupted]; neurological status from clinical examination [ ].
Non-contiguous fracture of [ ].
Paraspinal haematoma and associated [ ] injury.
steps.tip: Do not complete the TLICS neurological component from imaging; state the clinical status supplied.

steps.label: Site and side
steps.detail: Identify the exact bone and surface, including the tension or compression side where it matters.
steps.look: Radiographs and coronal and axial MRI for the exact bone and cortex involved.
steps.normal: No stress injury identified.
findings: Stress injury of the posteromedial tibial cortex (lower-risk site).
Stress injury on the tension (superolateral) side of the femoral neck (high-risk site).
Navicular stress fracture in the central third (high-risk site).
steps.tip: High-risk sites — femoral neck tension side, anterior tibial cortex, navicular, proximal fifth metatarsal and sesamoids — warrant prompt communication.

steps.label: Fracture line
steps.detail: Look for a cortical or trabecular fracture line and any displacement.
steps.look: T1 and fluid-sensitive images for a low-signal line; CT or radiographs for a cortical line such as the anterior tibial "dreaded black line".
steps.normal: No fracture line.
findings: Linear T1-hypointense fracture line extending __ mm into the [ ] without displacement.
Horizontal lucent line in the anterior tibial cortex.
Complete fracture with __ mm displacement.

steps.label: Marrow and periosteum
steps.detail: Separate periosteal oedema, marrow oedema and T1 marrow change, and note periosteal new bone.
steps.look: Fluid-sensitive images for periosteal and marrow oedema; T1 images for marrow change; radiographs for callus.
steps.normal: Normal marrow and periosteal signal.
findings: Periosteal oedema without marrow oedema (early stress reaction).
Periosteal and marrow oedema with T1 marrow change, without a fracture line.
Solid periosteal new bone and callus on radiographs.
steps.tip: Periosteal oedema alone is the earliest MRI finding; T1 marrow change and a visible line indicate a more advanced injury.

steps.label: Articular surface and soft tissues
steps.detail: Assess joint surface extension, collapse, effusion and adjacent soft tissues.
steps.look: Coronal and sagittal images through the adjacent joint.
steps.normal: No articular extension, collapse or effusion.
findings: Subchondral insufficiency fracture of the [femoral head / tibial plateau] with [no / __ mm] collapse.
Joint effusion.
Adjacent soft-tissue oedema.

steps.label: Comparison and differential
steps.detail: Compare evolution and consider insufficiency, infection or another lesion when the pattern is atypical.
steps.look: Prior radiographs and MRI; in an older patient or unusual site, consider insufficiency and an underlying lesion.
steps.normal: No underlying lesion; appearance typical of a fatigue stress injury.
findings: Healing since [date] with callus and reduced oedema.
Insufficiency fracture in osteopenic bone of the [ ].
Focal lesion underlying the fracture; a pathological fracture should be considered.

steps.label: Target and preprocedure survey
steps.detail: Confirm the named joint or bursa and assess fluid, anatomy and a safe route.
steps.look: Scan the target in two planes and use Doppler along the planned path; identify tendons and nerves to avoid.
steps.normal: Target identified on ultrasound; planned route clear of vessels, nerves and tendons on Doppler.
findings: Glenohumeral effusion of __ mm in the posterior recess; posterior approach selected.
Distended subacromial–subdeltoid bursa; lateral approach selected.
Vessel on the anterior approach on Doppler; alternative route chosen.
steps.tip: Confirm side and target at the time-out before skin preparation.

steps.label: Technique
steps.detail: Document patient position, sterile preparation, needle approach and local anaesthesia.
steps.look: Record position, approach (in-plane or out-of-plane), needle and anaesthetic actually used.
steps.normal: Aseptic technique with sterile probe cover and gel; in-plane needle approach under continuous ultrasound guidance.
findings: Patient [supine / lateral decubitus / prone]; [anterior / posterior / lateral] approach.
__ G, __ mm needle; local anaesthesia with __ mL of [agent, concentration].

steps.label: Needle tip and delivery
steps.detail: Confirm the needle tip location and the spread observed in the intended compartment.
steps.look: Keep the needle tip visible; confirm intra-articular or intrabursal spread in real time and save an image.
steps.normal: Needle tip confirmed within the target; injectate seen distending the intended compartment; image saved.
findings: Injected: __ mL of [corticosteroid, dose] with __ mL of [local anaesthetic, concentration].
Extra-articular spread observed; needle repositioned before completing the injection.

steps.label: Aspiration
steps.detail: Record the amount and appearance of any aspirate and the specimens actually sent.
steps.look: Aspirate before injecting when fluid is present; note volume and appearance.
steps.normal: Aspiration not performed.
findings: __ mL of [clear / straw-coloured / turbid / blood-stained / purulent] fluid aspirated.
Sent for [cell count, Gram stain and culture / crystal analysis] to [laboratory].
steps.tip: If the aspirate looks purulent, follow the local septic-joint pathway before any corticosteroid injection.

steps.label: Outcome and aftercare
steps.detail: Describe tolerance, immediate complication and the aftercare advice given.
steps.look: Record the immediate response and any complication before the patient leaves.
steps.normal: Procedure well tolerated; no immediate complication; aftercare advice given.
findings: Immediate pain relief after local anaesthetic (diagnostic response).
Vasovagal reaction, resolved with [ ].
Advised to seek urgent review for increasing pain, redness, swelling or fever.

steps.label: Carpal arcs (Gilula's lines)
steps.detail: Trace all three carpal arcs and check that the intercarpal joint spaces are parallel and symmetric.
steps.look: Neutral PA view: arc 1 along the proximal surfaces of the proximal row, arc 2 along its distal surfaces, arc 3 along the proximal capitate and hamate; intercarpal spaces normally about 1–2 mm.
steps.normal: Gilula's three carpal arcs are smooth and uninterrupted; intercarpal joint spaces are parallel and symmetric.
findings: Scapholunate interval widened to __ mm on the PA view, compatible with scapholunate ligament injury.
Break in arcs 1 and 2 at the lunate with a triangular lunate on the PA view (lunate or perilunate dislocation).
Scaphoid ring sign with a foreshortened scaphoid, indicating rotatory subluxation.
steps.tip: Compare the scapholunate interval with the other intercarpal spaces; clenched-fist views can unmask a dynamic injury.

steps.label: Lateral alignment
steps.detail: Assess the radius–lunate–capitate relationship on a true lateral view.
steps.look: True lateral (pisiform over the distal scaphoid pole): radius, lunate and capitate should be collinear.
steps.normal: Radius, lunate and capitate are collinear on the true lateral view.
findings: Perilunate dislocation: the lunate stays aligned with the radius while the capitate is dislocated dorsally.
Lunate dislocation: the lunate is tipped volarly out of the radial fossa while the capitate stays aligned with the radius.
Dorsal tilt of the lunate with a volar-flexed scaphoid (DISI pattern).
steps.tip: State which bone stays aligned with the radius: the lunate in perilunate dislocation, the capitate in lunate dislocation.

steps.label: Carpal angles
steps.detail: Measure the axes with stated landmarks and describe a DISI or VISI pattern where supported.
steps.look: True lateral: scaphoid axis along its volar poles, lunate axis perpendicular to the line joining its horns, and the capitate and radius axes.
steps.normal: Scapholunate and capitolunate angles within normal limits; no DISI or VISI pattern.
findings: Scapholunate angle __° (above 60°) with dorsal lunate tilt: DISI.
Scapholunate angle __° (below 30°) with volar lunate tilt: VISI.
Angles not reliably measurable because of [rotation / cast].
steps.tip: The normal scapholunate angle is about 30–60°; angles need a true lateral projection.

steps.label: Bones
steps.detail: Inspect for associated carpal or distal forearm fracture and chronic collapse.
steps.look: Scaphoid views for waist fractures; lunate density; distal radius and ulnar styloid.
steps.normal: No carpal or distal forearm fracture; scaphoid and lunate normal in shape and density.
findings: Scaphoid waist fracture [displaced __ mm / with humpback deformity].
Scaphoid non-union with sclerosis and cysts; proximal pole sclerosis raises concern for osteonecrosis.
Increased density and collapse of the lunate (Kienböck disease).

steps.label: Degenerative and dynamic findings
steps.detail: Map arthrosis and compare neutral with stress views.
steps.look: PA and lateral for radioscaphoid and capitolunate arthrosis; clenched-fist or deviation views when acquired.
steps.normal: No arthrosis; no dynamic change on stress views, or stress views not acquired.
findings: Scapholunate advanced collapse (SLAC) pattern: radial styloid–scaphoid then capitolunate arthrosis, with the radiolunate joint preserved.
Scapholunate interval widens from __ mm to __ mm on the clenched-fist view (dynamic instability).
Scaphoid non-union advanced collapse (SNAC) pattern.

steps.label: Fracture morphology
steps.detail: Identify the bone, level, articular extension and comminution.
steps.look: PA, lateral and oblique views: distal radius, ulnar styloid, then each carpal bone — scaphoid first.
steps.normal: No fracture of the distal radius, ulna or carpal bones.
findings: Extra-articular distal radius fracture __ cm proximal to the articular surface with dorsal angulation (Colles type).
Intra-articular distal radius fracture extending to the radiocarpal joint [and distal radioulnar joint], with comminution.
Ulnar styloid [tip / base] fracture.
Torus (buckle) fracture of the distal radial metaphysis.
steps.tip: Eponyms are optional; direction of displacement and articular involvement are what matter.

steps.label: Displacement
steps.detail: Describe angulation, translation and shortening with clear directions.
steps.look: True lateral for palmar or dorsal tilt; PA for radial inclination, radial height and ulnar variance.
steps.normal: Normal radial inclination, radial height and palmar tilt; no shortening.
findings: Dorsal tilt of __° (normal palmar tilt about 11°); radial inclination __°; radial height __ mm.
Dorsal translation of __ mm and radial shortening with positive ulnar variance of __ mm.
Volar displacement of the distal fragment (Smith type).
steps.tip: Radial shortening over 3 mm, dorsal tilt beyond 10° or an articular step over 2 mm are commonly used thresholds for unacceptable alignment.

steps.label: Articular surface
steps.detail: Assess radiocarpal and distal radioulnar congruity.
steps.look: Lateral and PA views for step and gap; CT for a depressed lunate facet and sigmoid notch involvement.
steps.normal: Radiocarpal and distal radioulnar articular surfaces congruent.
findings: Articular step of __ mm and gap of __ mm at the [scaphoid / lunate] fossa.
Depressed lunate facet (die-punch) fragment, __ mm.
[Volar / dorsal] rim fracture with carpal subluxation (Barton type).
Radial styloid fracture extending to the scaphoid fossa.

steps.label: Carpal alignment
steps.detail: Assess fracture-associated subluxation, the carpal arcs and ligamentous avulsion clues.
steps.look: Carpal arcs on the PA view; lunate and capitate alignment on the lateral; scapholunate interval.
steps.normal: Carpal alignment normal; scapholunate interval normal.
findings: Associated scapholunate widening of __ mm.
Perilunate instability pattern with a [trans-scaphoid] fracture.
Dorsal triquetral avulsion fracture on the lateral view.
steps.tip: A dorsal flake behind the proximal carpal row on the lateral view is usually a triquetral avulsion.

steps.label: Reduction and soft tissues
steps.detail: Describe interval reduction, fixation and soft-tissue swelling.
steps.look: Compare with the pre-reduction film, including cast and fixation.
steps.normal: Soft tissues otherwise unremarkable; no cast or fixation.
findings: Post-reduction: dorsal tilt improved from __° to __°; radial height __ mm.
Volar plate fixation with screws [not] penetrating the radiocarpal joint.
Loss of reduction since [date].
